blog_summary: The blog post discusses MacroBase, a system developed by Peter Bailis and collaborators at Cambridge Mobile Telematics (CMT) for analytic monitoring in IoT scenarios. The system focuses on detecting anomalies (outliers) in high-velocity data streams while balancing scale and timeliness. Adrian Colyer highlights MacroBase's novel combination of robust statistical estimation with streaming data structures, enabling interactive exploration and high-performance deployment (up to 1M points per second on a single core). The paper emphasizes careful system design, leveraging prior art, and adapting techniques to new problems. MacroBase ingests multi-dimensional data streams, automatically applies outlier detection and summarization, and supports both batch and streaming queries with exponentially decayed windows. The system targets the 'sweet spot' between obvious failures and rare events, where manual inspection is impractical. The author praises the system's thoughtful design, minimal codebase (7,000 lines), and practical impact, including finding unknown bugs in production systems at CMT.
paper_title: MacroBase: Analytic Monitoring for the Internet of Things

This process, which we call analytic monitoring, is at the core of many IoT applications, including equipment monitoring (e.g., detecting failing manufacturing componentry), intrusion detection (e.g., building break-ins), and environmental observation (e.g., occupancy and HVAC control). In these applications, analytic monitoring is critical to reliability, efficiency, and observability. Moreover, their i.) extreme scale (hundreds of thousands to millions of complex events per second) and ii.) demands for timely (i.e., minutes to seconds or shorter) yet complex statistical analysis pose serious challenges for existing data analysis infrastructure. An increasing proportion of data today is generated by automated processes, sensors, and systems—collectively, the Internet of Things (IoT). A key challenge in IoT data management and a core aspect of many IoT applications (e.g., industrial diagnostics, predictive maintenance, and equipment auditing) is in identifying and highlighting unusual and surprising data (e.g., poor driving behavior, equipment failures, physical intrusion). We call this task, which is often statistical in nature and time-sensitive, analytic monitoring. To facilitate rapid development and scalable deployment of analytic monitoring queries, we have developed MacroBase, a data analytics engine that performs analytic monitoring of IoT data streams. MacroBase implements a customizable pipeline of outlier detection, summarization, and ranking operators. For efficient and accurate execution, MacroBase implements several cross-layer optimizations across robust estimation, pattern mining, and sketching procedures, allowing order-of-magnitude speedups.
